Hi all,

Quick technical primer / answers so we can scope the kickoff properly:

1) CIDR & peering model
- Preferred Redwood VPC CIDR block for peering: 10.18.0.0/16 (we can accommodate alternate ranges if there is overlap; we prefer /16 for future tenancy).
- Peering is single-directional for control plane traffic; data plane uses private endpoints (see below).

2) Allowlist / egress IPs
- For initial allowlisting please include the following egress IP ranges (us-east-1): 3.12.45.0/24, 3.12.46.0/24.
- If you require static egress from the appliance, we can provide an EIP assignment for the on-prem box (request during provisioning).

3) Ports / protocols
- 443 (HTTPS, TLS1.2+) — primary for API traffic and private endpoints (required)
- 10250 (gRPC health/metrics) — optional but recommended for Ops insights (allow only from Redwood IPs)
- 8143 (internal agent sync) — used for appliance management during install (we open during provisioning window only)

4) Private endpoints
- We'll provision cross-account ENIs in your VPC (us-east-1) for private API endpoints. Private DNS will be used so app traffic resolves to the private interfaces.

5) On-prem package requirements
- Appliance: 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, 500 GB NVMe (recommended); VMware/Hyper-V images also supported (OVA available).
- Network: dual-homed NICs (one for management, one for data), outbound TLS egress allowed to Redwood egress ranges above.
- Ship time: standard fulfillment is 7-10 business days from SOW execution; expedited options are available.

6) Cutover/maintenance window
- We prefer a 3-hour window (evening US-EAST) for initial peering + DNS cutover; we'll coordinate runbook and rollback steps.

I dropped a short implementation risks spreadsheet into the shared drive (implementation-risk-register.xlsx) outlining dependency owners.

Happy to go into any of these on the kickoff.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Network & Deployments Lead, Redwood Inference
